name: Ricardo J. Gowdie
title: Ricardo J. Gowdie, IT Infrastructure Engineer
description: IT infrastructure engineer in Fayetteville, NC. I plan, design and build infrastructure that stays up: clusters, backups, cloud, identity and networks.
availability: Available for remote or hybrid consulting and freelance projects on Eastern Time.

hero.headline: I plan, design and build IT infrastructure that stays up.
hero.subline: I've worked in IT since 2009 and in enterprise environments since 2017. I take on consulting projects and infrastructure work: failover clusters, backups, cloud, identity, and the networks that tie them together. Let's talk about yours.

certifications: Data Protection (University of the West Indies)
Cisco IT Essentials I and II (Cisco Networking Academy)
education: BSc (Hons.) Information Technology, University of Technology, Jamaica

approach.title: Plan
approach.text: I start with what the business needs and what is already there, then agree on what done looks like.

approach.title: Design
approach.text: I draw it out, weigh the options, and write down why I chose one.

approach.title: Build
approach.text: I build it in stages, test failover and restores, and keep a rollback ready.

approach.title: Run
approach.text: I leave runbooks and monitoring so the next person doesn't start from zero.

personalNote: I got into IT because I have a knack for connecting things and making them work together. That started in Jamaica in 2009. Today I work from Fayetteville, NC.

steps.title: Train and mentor
steps.text: I train and mentor support staff on troubleshooting, escalation, and documentation.

steps.title: Own the incident
steps.text: I own high-priority incidents from start to finish and keep stakeholders informed until they're resolved.

steps.title: Work with vendors
steps.text: I work with vendors and managed service providers to fix problems.

steps.title: Write it down
steps.text: I write runbooks so the next person doesn't start from zero.

closing.headline: Planning an infrastructure project? Let's talk it through.
